ai.description: *Hylarana caesari* is a slender frog (35–45 mm) with a golden-brown dorsum and distinct white upper lip. It features a dark lateral band and prominent dorsolateral folds extending from the snout to vent.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Hylarana caesari* is best distinguished by the presence of a distinct, continuous white or cream-colored line running along its upper lip, which is absent in similar species.
ai.habitat: *Hylarana caesari* inhabits evergreen and semi-evergreen forests in the northern Western Ghats, typically found near rocky streams at elevations between 400 and 1,000 meters.
ai.behavior: The Maharashtra Golden-backed Frog is primarily nocturnal, often found perched on low vegetation near forest streams where it actively hunts for small insects.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Hylarana caesari* breeds during the monsoon, laying large clutches of approximately 400–600 eggs in gelatinous masses attached to submerged vegetation in forest streams.
ai.distributionRemarks: The Maharashtra Golden-backed Frog is endemic to the northern Western Ghats, primarily occurring in the states of Maharashtra and Goa at mid-to-high elevations.
ai.callDescription: The Maharashtra Golden-backed Frog produces a series of short, high-pitched "tink" notes, typically heard calling from vegetation near forest streams during the monsoon.
